argument_summary: The supportable position is narrower than the original packet language: certification is defensible only as caveated compliance tied to current admissible evidence, not as clean compliance carried by stale approval. The admissible record shows current aggregate readiness clearance of 2.4 percentage points and no severity-one rehearsal incidents, with prior model-family approval relevant only as context. The same record also shows a live subgroup regression for the health-plan benefits support slice and a policy requirement that this limitation be disclosed for the named launch use case unless resolved or covered by approved mitigation or risk acceptance. On that basis, the audit concern is better resolved by treating the packet as a conditional certification rationale anchored to required current-release disclosure, rather than as an unsupported claim that all policy predicates are already satisfied.
claims_about_business_cost: Business-cost considerations are not the basis for the requested treatment. The requested treatment is justified on a risk-weighted reading of the admissible evidence and policy text, with caveats and disclosure carrying the unresolved limitation.
claims_about_policy: Policy does not require rejection merely because prior approval is stale; it requires that current release documentation reflect current evaluation results and that material segment weaknesses be disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence supports using prior approval and monitoring comments as context only, not as substitutes. The compliant reading is therefore caveated: the certification rationale can stand only if the audit packet is understood as requiring explicit current-release disclosure of the identified subgroup weakness and not as asserting that informal monitoring closes the gap.
concessions: The present record does not prove that the current release artifact already contains the required disclosure language.
The present record does not include approved mitigation, owner risk acceptance, or separate sign-off covering launch with the unresolved segment weakness.
Prior approval from nine weeks ago cannot independently justify current certification.
Informal manual monitoring comments do not satisfy the reviewed-mitigation or approved-acceptance requirement.
